reason: The hypothesis directly transfers the boron-addition strategy and its mechanism (intergranular boride precipitation for ductility improvement) from the HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy studied in P12, P18, P20, P22, P23, and P29 to the NbMoTaW alloy. The core idea, mechanism, and predicted outcome are taken almost verbatim from these passages, with only the target alloy changed. The proposed irradiation benefit is a minor extension of the known defect-sink role of second phases (P5) but is not substantiated by any new mechanistic link or evidence specific to NbMoTaW.
copied_elements: Adding ~0.1 at.% boron to a refractory high-entropy alloy
Formation of nanoscale boride precipitates at grain boundaries
Change in fracture mode from intergranular to transgranular
BCC matrix remains intact for high-temperature strength
